points.text: Definition 2.3 leaves +1 position unspecified; operator not canonical, invariance not established.
Smoothness theorem false for cells of three or more nodes; proof assumes graph Laplacian.
Positive-definiteness desideratum conflicts with extending the singular graph Laplacian.
Hodge Laplacian comparison is a straw man; no rank-to-rank or up/down Laplacian comparison.
Cell structure of the counterexample is not stated in text.
Equal expressiveness on simplicial complexes in Corollary 4.2 asserted without argument.
Related work omits hypergraph Laplacians and hypergraph neural networks.
Related work omits spectral/diffusion positional encodings for graph transformers.
Contribution narrower than claimed; higher-rank cells barely affect the Laplacian.
Corollary cited before definition; transpose inconsistency between Eq. 3 and Theorem 8.3.
Statement about rank-1 kernel contradicts descriptor defined on rank-0 cells.
Expressivity theorem conflates orthogonal similarity with isomorphism; proof shows wrong direction.
Universal approximation corollary ignores permutation invariance over nodes.
No ablation isolating HKS descriptor from transformer or alternative encodings.
Claim that only CC Laplacian works, not Hodge, reported without numbers.
MLP-Mixer claim has no numbers; backbone per Table 3 cell unclear.
Expressivity benchmark self-built and circular by construction against SMCN.
No trivial per-rank counting baseline for expressivity task.
Expressivity metric undefined (0% accuracy) and dataset details missing.
Gains small relative to reported noise; number of runs unstated.
State-of-the-art wording unsupported given ties and losses.
MolHIV metric labelled ACC rather than ROC-AUC.
Stronger graph-transformer baselines on MolHIV absent.
CIN failing to learn suggests untuned baseline.
Timing mixes units and does not state what is timed.
Constant-footprint scalability claim tested only up to 100 cells, contradicts limitations.
'12 times faster' claim not reproducible from Table 3.
Table 1 marks SMCN scalable contrary to Section 5.2.
Hyperparameters, training details and baseline provenance missing.
6,000 GPU hours unexplained; extent of hyperparameter search unclear.
Code only promised after acceptance.
Equation, figure and section cross-references wrong.
Typos in Table 3 caption.
Maximal expressivity claim contradicted by cospectral counterexamples; proofs conflate orthogonal similarity.
Laplacian depends on unspecified +1 position.
Constant function has nonzero energy, contradicting smoothness theorem.
Expressivity test circular, built around SMCN's rank limit.
Expressivity metric (0% accuracy) undefined.
No trivial baseline for expressivity test.
State-of-the-art claim unsupported by results.
Scalability and constant-footprint claims unsupported beyond 100 cells.
'12 times faster' claim not supported by tables.
No control separating HKS from backbone, feature map or hyperparameter search.
Hodge comparison straw man; rank-to-rank and hypergraph Laplacians not compared.
Table 1 marks SMCN scalable contrary to text.
Permutation-equivariant vs permutation-invariant inconsistency.
Wrong equation, figure and section cross-references.
Known limits of HKS diagonal not discussed; conflicts with maximal expressivity claim.
Small high-rank weights make claimed sensitivity to high-rank cells numerically weak.
Cubic eigendecomposition cost unanalysed; approximate heat-kernel methods not discussed.
No evaluation on large complexes beyond 100 cells.
Assumes given meaningful rank labels; experiments use graphs without higher-rank cells.
Broader-impact applications named without evidence.
Future-work items lack a first small experiment.
Performance claims inconsistent across abstract, introduction and results.
Permutation-equivariant vs permutation-invariant inconsistency.
Theory presented as sketches; orthogonal matrix where permutation expected; may not hold.
Expressivity evidence limited to one author-built dataset.
No ablation of HKS over transformer alone or standard positional encodings.
MLP-Mixer discussion has no numbers.
Wrong equation and figure cross-references; corollary cited before existing.
Table 3 mixes seconds and iterations per second.
Typos in Table 3 caption.
MolHIV metric labelled ACC.
Cannot distinguish isospectral non-isomorphic complexes; expressiveness limitation.
Eigendecomposition bottleneck for large complexes; Nystrom approximation not implemented.
Evaluation limited to classification tasks.
No ablations or visualisations of what HKS descriptors capture.
No comparison against standard graph HKS to isolate CC benefit.
Missing related work on Fourier/wavelet multi-scale spectral descriptors.
Theory section too long and largely known results.
Experiments not comprehensive, especially on higher-order complexes.
No experiments verifying theory or comparing Hodge vs CC Laplacian performance.
Unspecified open questions remain.
Unclear passages, typos and missing definitions hamper readability.
Theoretical results trivial, misleading or possibly incorrect.
Datasets are small.
Comparisons incomplete.

P.summary: Laplacian definition non-canonical due to unspecified +1 sign position.
Smoothness theorem false for larger cells.
Hodge Laplacian comparison is a straw man.
High-rank cells contribute little; contribution narrower than claimed.
Main expressivity theorem flawed: orthogonal similarity not isomorphism.
Universal approximation corollary ignores permutation invariance.
No ablation isolating HKS descriptor contribution.
Hodge vs CC Laplacian claim without numbers.
Expressivity benchmark self-built, single and circular.
No trivial counting baseline for expressivity.
Scalability claims unsupported; eigendecomposition cost and large-scale tests missing.
Unexplained 6,000 GPU hours and search extent.
Known spectral limits of HKS not discussed.
Rank labels assumed; no realistic higher-rank structure tested.

Q.summary: Eigendecomposition scalability bottleneck; approximations not evaluated.
No ablation or visualisation of HKS descriptors.
No comparison with standard graph HKS.
Theory section overlong and mostly known.
Experiments limited: small datasets, few higher-order complexes.
No empirical Hodge vs CC Laplacian comparison or theory verification.
Theoretical results trivial, misleading or incorrect.
